title: Eritrea follow-up evidence — 5 November 2026
purpose: Record current 2026 crop-season risk and reconcile official Ministry of Agriculture output reporting before any calculator mapping.

fao_giews_2026_09_30.source: FAO GIEWS Country Brief, reference date 30 September 2026
findings: 2026 main-season planting of wheat, barley, sorghum, maize, teff and pulses was completed in July in central and western Anseba, Debub, Maekel and Gash Barka.
June–September 2026 Kiremti rainfall in those regions was 20–40 percent below average.
FAO reports significant vegetation stress, including Gash Barka, the country's main crop-producing region, and expects significant crop production shortfalls.
fao_giews_2026_09_30.decision: Treat 2026 production as a weather-risk season; do not use historical national cereal averages as current 2026 yield assumptions or project current yields without crop/region observations.

ministry_2024_reporting.source: Eritrea Ministry of Information / Ministry of Agriculture annual activity assessment, 1 February 2025
findings: The report states that more than 414,000 hectares of land were cultivated in 2024, including over 38,000 hectares of various crops and around 60,000 hectares of oilseed crops; cereals reportedly increased 138 percent year-on-year.

The related Ministry technical summary dated 7 February 2025 states that 414,000 hectares were cultivated with cereals, over half sorghum, followed by pearl millet, teff, wheat, finger millet, barley and maize; it separately reports 60,000 hectares of oil crops and 38,000 hectares of pulses.

The 7 February report states 67,000 tonnes of fruits and 182,000 tonnes of vegetables harvested from 4,800 and 14,000 hectares respectively; the 1 February report instead displays 67 tonnes and 182 tonnes, creating a 1,000-fold unit discrepancy.
The 2024 report records more than one million livestock vaccinations, not livestock inventory or enterprise output.
ministry_2024_reporting.qualification: The Ministry's two contemporaneous public reports are not fully consistent in land-use wording and fruit/vegetable units. Do not use the 414,000-ha figure as a definitive crop-specific area or the horticulture totals as validated calculator yields until original tables and definitions are obtained.

ministry_2025_campaign_update.source: Eritrea Ministry of Information / Ministry of Agriculture, 25 August 2025
findings: By the first week of August 2025, more than 384,000 hectares had been ploughed and planted; this was a season-progress snapshot and was expected to increase.
More than 40,800 hectares were planted using Azmera rainfall and spate irrigation.
Vegetables were reported on approximately 10,870 hectares and fruits on more than 5,000 hectares, with estimated output reported as 145 tonnes of vegetables and 63 tonnes of fruits.
ministry_2025_campaign_update.qualification: The area is a mid-season progress figure, not final harvested area; production estimates require clarification of coverage and units.

world_bank_indicators.source: World Bank WDI, secondary indicator display

cereal_yield.qualification: National cereal aggregate only; not a crop-specific yield or regional enterprise assumption.

arable_land.qualification: National arable land, not crop harvested area.

fertilizer_use.qualification: National fertilizer nutrient intensity, not product prices or farm application rates.

inputs_and_markets.finding: IFAD describes higher fertilizer and fuel costs, reduced input use, and interventions to improve local seed production and access to inputs.
inputs_and_markets.qualification: No validated unit prices, crop-specific application costs or farmgate prices extracted.

next_actions: Obtain the underlying Ministry of Agriculture 2024 regional crop statistics and resolve the 414,000-ha land-use classification discrepancy.
Verify whether the fruit and vegetable outputs in the February 2025 Ministry reports are tonnes or thousand tonnes.
Extract crop- and region-specific 2024 production and harvested area for sorghum, millet, teff, wheat, barley, maize, pulses, vegetables and supported livestock.
Locate dated farmgate prices by crop, market, grade and unit; do not substitute Asmara wholesale or retail prices.
Obtain farmer-paid seed, fertilizer, crop protection, fuel, labour, machinery and irrigation rates by region.
Account for FAO's September 2026 drought warning when selecting a season or yield baseline.
